_README: B6 Studios — the ONE config for this client (base + this file = the B6 instance). COMPILED by server/render.py. Corrected for the Instantly model: the sending identity (from-name, from-address, sending domains, warmup, tracked links) is set INSIDE the Instantly workspace, NOT here. Apollo sources leads; Instantly sends. Keys live in .secrets/mcp_state.json, provided at runtime. Unknowns are null and listed under _needs_from_client — never fabricated.

company.name: B6 Studios
company.mission: Brands own a show, not an ad. B6 builds episodic branded series for TikTok, Reels, and Shorts — content people come back to watch.
company.context: B6 builds shows for brands. Instead of one-off social posts that disappear, B6 creates episodic series (TikTok / Reels / Shorts) that audiences return to — brands stop interrupting audiences and start entertaining them. TWO MODELS: (1) Sponsor an existing creator series (creators who already have audience/engagement — Teddy Alvarez-Nissen / 7 Stories, Chewkz / Surviving the Cows) — a brand associates with proven content; used as LIVE PROOF. (2) Co-develop a custom branded series — the brand funds it, B6 produces it, the brand gets its own season. LEAD WITH MODEL 2; use model 1 as proof. TAM LOGIC: any consumer brand doing roughly $20M+ revenue can afford this and should be experimenting with episodic short-form, because that is where attention is moving. THE PITCH IS NOT 'buy an ad' — IT IS 'own a show.' This general engine sells the wide net (model 2); it is separate from Avi's manual sniper pipelines.
company.scope_rules: GENERAL outreach only — the wide net. HARD GUARDRAILS: (1) NEVER touch Surviving the Cows, Trashed, or 7 Stories named targets — those are Avi's manual sniper pipelines; dedupe against the dedupe/ lists before every send. (2) NEVER send from b6studios.com or mason@b6studios.com — sending is via the Instantly SDR cold-domain account (the from-identity is configured IN Instantly). (3) Match the ask to seniority: director level and above; never aim a six-figure 'own a show' concept at a coordinator. (4) No invented facts, no fabricated revenue figures or stats — use only approved numbers. (5) A brand with no real social presence cannot be a good fit regardless of other signals (active-in-social is B6's explicit near-gate).

departments.name: lead_gen
departments.purpose: Source and qualify ICP-matched consumer brands via Apollo; turn the raw count into a qualified TAM using the B6 rubric.

targeting.notes: Consumer-facing brands ~$20M+ revenue that already make content or obviously should, with a product/world a short-form series could be built around. Never aim a six-figure concept at a coordinator.

market_crosscheck.note: consumer-brand NAICS (food/beverage/apparel/toiletries/clothing-retail) as a STARTER ICP approximation — refine which NAICS truly match.

icp_rubric.instruction: Score each pulled account 0-100 (ADDITIVE — never multiply). Output per account {tier, score, reason}. Calibrate against B6's actual closed-won when loaded; until then score the SPEC ICP and mark uncertainty honestly.

criteria.earns: posting regularly, multiple active accounts, real follower base, and especially creator/influencer/UGC partnerships (others organically promoting the brand — the single strongest 'active' signal)
sells to consumers; a product/world a short-form series could be built around
the product naturally lives inside an episodic format

tiers.note: A/B = good fit (drive qualified-TAM rate). Active-in-social is a near-gate: no real social presence -> cap at C and flag.

anti_pitfalls: size counted once (revenue/headcount/'big' co-vary — one axis)
missing data != poor fit (lean C, note the gap, never a confident 0)
the reason paragraph IS the audit trail
icp_rubric.out_of_scope: anything on the dedupe/ lists (STC / Trashed / 7 Stories), the primary domain, B2B-only / non-consumer, or sub-director contacts aimed at a six-figure concept -> tier D / skip

departments.name: outreach
departments.purpose: Run the cold campaign via Instantly (the SDR sending account). Personalized four-part sends that make a director+ brand marketer book a 15-minute call.

config.goal: Make a director-level-or-above brand marketer book a 15-minute call with Mason and Weston. The reader's reaction must be 'this is the most interesting inbound I have ever received.'

four_part_anatomy: a. Real proof up top — a link to a real performing B6/creator episode (the video is the conversion tool; goes early, is real).

b. Brand-specific hook — one specific observational line about the brand's recent content/launch/campaign (not flattery), then a short scene placing THIS brand's actual product inside one of our show-worlds (reader does zero imaginative work = hyper-personalized).

c. (video variant only, later) AI mockup teaser framed honestly — 'we mocked this up to show the idea; our artists do the real production.' General lane only; never on a premium named target; never imply the brand was involved.
d. One low-friction CTA — 15 minutes with Mason and Weston, the calendar link, nothing else (no pricing/deck/attachments in touch one).
hard_rules: Body under 170 words; short and direct, no filler.
Custom subject line naming the brand; never generic.
No em dashes, no en dashes (periods/commas/plain hyphens only). No emojis.
No artificial urgency or fake deadlines; scarcity only if real (category exclusivity).
Use ONLY numbers that appear verbatim in approved assets; if not given a stat, use no stat.
First line of the body = the recipient's email address (QA copy/paste rule).

Signature/sender identity: SET IN INSTANTLY (the SDR sending account). Do NOT send from b6studios.com. The in-body sign-off + booking parties (Mason/Weston) are an open client decision — see _needs_from_client.sender_identity.

cadence.purpose: proof the format works (approved examples + approved B6 numbers); re-link the page
budget reframe: you already spend on social; here is how it compounds into owned IP. First soft meeting ask.
short breakup: 'Closing the loop on [Brand].' Door left open.

subject_options: What [Brand] looks like as a series
[Brand] keeps posting. We made you a show instead.
copy.brand_colors: navy blue + chartreuse green (client-facing, when branding appears)

compliance.note: CAN-SPAM requires a real physical address + a working unsubscribe link. Confirm whether Instantly injects these or B6 supplies them; a live send is blocked until both are resolved.

_needs_from_client.instantly.INSTANTLY_API_KEY: API key of the WARMED Instantly workspace (the SDR sending account — from-name, sending domains, warmup, tracked links are all configured in Instantly). Confirm: is there a warmed Instantly campaign (⇒ we need its api key + campaign_id), or is warmup on SMTP domains (⇒ different, longer path)?
_needs_from_client.outreach.instantly_campaign_ref: the Instantly campaign id to load leads into / start.
_needs_from_client.apollo.APOLLO_API_KEY: Apollo API key for lead search + qualification.
_needs_from_client.sender_identity: the SDR sending persona (from-name/from-address in Instantly, NOT mason@b6studios.com) AND whether the body still signs off / books as Mason + Weston. This is B6/Avi's call — do not fabricate.
_needs_from_client.outreach.compliance.postal_address: a real physical mailing address for the CAN-SPAM footer (or confirm Instantly injects it).
_needs_from_client.outreach.compliance.unsubscribe_url: a working unsubscribe link (or confirm Instantly injects it).
_needs_from_client.booking_calendar_url: the Mason + Weston 15-minute booking link for the CTA.
_needs_from_client.proof_assets: the real performing B6/creator episode links + approved facts/numbers the copy may cite (nothing else may be cited).
